note: Independent sources (SupremeToday, TaxConcept/TaxGuru, and NCLAT's own cause-list notice listing the two connected appeals, Comp. App. (AT)(Ins) Nos. 1138 and 1145 of 2026) show the corporate debtor NCLT Ahmedabad admitted into liquidation on 10 October 2025 was Honest Derivatives (Private) Limited, not Garden Court Distilleries. Garden Court Distilleries was the successful going-concern auction purchaser of Honest Derivatives, seeking implementation reliefs in appeal 1145; it was never itself in liquidation. The draft has these two entities' roles reversed throughout its body (it treats Garden Court Distilleries as the liquidated company). The underlying legal point (regulations governing a going-concern sale are fixed as of the Section 33 liquidation order date, not a later IBBI amendment) and the NCLAT's ruling allowing the appeal and remanding within two weeks appear to be real, but the draft's factual account of who was liquidated and who was the buyer is materially wrong -- this needs a rewrite, not isolated find/replace fixes. Note also: the NCLAT bench is reported as Justice Yogesh Khanna (Officiating Chairperson) with Technical Members Barun Mitra and Ajai Das Mehrotra, which the draft also left unconfirmed.
